claim: Every financial asset in a macroeconomic system is intrinsically another sector liability and the sum of all net financial assets across all sectors equals zero
support: Godley and Lavoie demonstrate that in a closed financial system every asset has a counterpart liability so the sum of all net financial claims is identically zero: Sum Delta NW_j = 0
limitations: Post-Keynesian structural assumption assumes closed economy accounting

claim: Stock-flow consistent models track all monetary transactions via a transaction-flow matrix where column sums equal zero ensuring no black hole money leakage
support: Transaction-flow matrices enforce that every inflow to one institutional sector represents an equal outflow from another sector ensuring zero leakage
limitations: Literature survey of theoretical models

claim: Discrete simulation ticks with explicit Euler or Runge-Kutta numerical damping maintain real-time 60fps stability without numerical explosion
support: Numerical solvers with value clamping and finite difference damping prevent runaway debt loops during extreme slider input spikes
limitations: Linearization reduces extreme non-linear tail shock precision

claim: Modern central banks manage short-term interest rates via interest on reserves and conduct open market asset purchases to expand liquidity
support: The Federal Reserve targets the federal funds rate corridor using interest on reserve balances and adjusts balance sheet size via asset purchases and rolloffs
limitations: Focuses primarily on US institutional mechanics

claim: Empirical monetary policy reaction functions follow Taylor-type rules responding systematically to inflation gaps and output gaps
support: Optimal control and empirical policy rules in FRB/US set the policy interest rate as a linear combination of the equilibrium real rate inflation gap and output gap
exact_location: FEDS Note Page 3 Policy Reaction Functions
limitations: Taylor rule coefficients assume stable long-run neutral interest rates

claim: Commercial banks create money endogenously in the form of bank deposits whenever they originate new loans rather than acting as mere intermediaries of pre-existing savings
support: Bank lending creates new deposits; whenever a bank makes a loan it simultaneously creates a matching deposit in the borrower bank account thereby creating new money
exact_location: Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin Page 14
limitations: Analysis focuses on commercial bank credit money excluding non-bank financial intermediaries

claim: Commercial bank loan growth is constrained by capital adequacy requirements profitability expectations and credit risk rather than central bank reserve multipliers
support: Bank lending is limited by regulatory capital ratios (Basel III) risk-adjusted net interest margins and borrower creditworthiness rather than reserve scarcity
exact_location: BIS Paper 86 Section 2 Bank Balance Sheets
limitations: Cross-country heterogeneity in regulatory enforcement

claim: Corporate enterprise value is the discounted present value of expected future free cash flows to the firm discounted at the weighted average cost of capital
support: DCF valuation equates enterprise value to the sum of discounted forecast cash flows plus terminal value where higher discount rates compress corporate valuations
exact_location: Economic Educational Tools Corporate Finance Section
independence_group: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
limitations: DCF models are highly sensitive to perpetual growth rate and discount rate assumptions

claim: Higher policy interest rates increase corporate borrowing costs widen credit spreads reduce debt service coverage and suppress corporate capital expenditure
support: Monetary tightening passes through into corporate bond yields raising debt service payments and depressing business fixed investment
limitations: Transmission lag varies between 6 and 18 months in empirical data

claim: Household consumption is driven by disposable wage income wealth effects from asset valuations and borrowing capacity
support: Consumer spending correlates positively with labor income and net household wealth while rising debt service ratios depress discretionary expenditures
exact_location: FRED Series PCE and Disposable Personal Income
independence_group: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
limitations: Aggregate data masks income inequality differences in marginal propensity to consume

claim: Credit expansion enables household spending to exceed income during cycle upswings while debt service burdens force spending below income during deleveraging
support: When credit is readily available spending grows faster than income during deleveraging debt service forces spending below income creating recessions
exact_location: How The Economic Machine Works Video Section 2 Short-Term Debt Cycle
limitations: Heuristic conceptual framework rather than econometric regression

claim: Government fiscal deficits create a corresponding net financial surplus for the private sector in a stock-flow consistent closed economy
support: The government budget balance identically equals the net private sector balance plus the foreign balance: (G - T) = (S - I) - NX
limitations: Assumes sovereign currency issuer with floating exchange rate

claim: Sovereign debt issuance expands the stock of risk-free liquid collateral in financial markets influencing term premia and bond yields
support: Heavy Treasury supply issuances interact with central bank asset holdings to determine sovereign yield curve slopes and term premiums
exact_location: Chapter 7 Fiscal Policy and Government Debt
limitations: Sovereign risk premium is assumed zero for US Treasury benchmark

claim: Bond prices exhibit negative convexity with respect to interest rate yields where duration measures first-order price sensitivity
support: The yield curve term structure reprices bonds instantaneously when benchmark rates shift where longer duration bonds experience larger price swings
exact_location: BIS Paper 86 Section 4 Financial Market Transmission
limitations: High-frequency liquidity shocks can temporarily distort theoretical convexity

claim: Asset prices in financial markets are determined by continuous double auction matching of buyers and sellers exchanging money and credit for financial assets
support: Financial markets clear at the equilibrium price where bid orders and ask orders cross with total transaction value equaling money plus credit paid
exact_location: How The Economic Machine Works Page 2 Transactions
limitations: Qualitative transaction framework requires order book depth queue calibration

claim: Interactive visual manipulations with zero-latency response (<16ms) dramatically increase user comprehension and retention of complex scientific and economic systems
support: Brilliant.org learning design shows that active manipulation of sliders and direct visual feedback creates deeper mental models than passive reading
limitations: Qualitative educational assessment without formal longitudinal clinical trial

claim: Educational economic simulations benefit from preset historical scenarios that allow learners to replicate known policy dilemmas and crises
support: St. Louis Fed Econ Lowdown tools use historical crisis scenarios (Great Depression 2008 Financial Crisis) to benchmark user decisions against historical reality
independence_group: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
limitations: Scenario presets must be simplified for pedagogical clarity

claim: Modeling short-term and long-term debt cycle deleveragings requires simultaneous tracking of spending debt relief austerity and money printing
support: A beautiful deleveraging balances spending cuts debt restructuring wealth transfers and central bank money printing to bring debt-to-income down without hyperinflation
exact_location: Section 4 Deleveragings and The Beautiful Deleveraging
limitations: Historical case studies primarily draw from 20th century developed market crises

claim: Dynamic T-accounts showing instantaneous asset and liability changes eliminate confusion regarding where monetary transfers originate and terminate
support: SFC model visual representations use T-account balance sheets to visually demonstrate balance sheet expansion and contraction across sectors
limitations: Requires clean screen layout to prevent multi-column information crowding

claim: Monochromatic broadsheet design with high-contrast typography and subtle animated flow lines focuses learner attention on causal connections rather than decorative noise
support: Minimizing gratuitous color and using structured typographic hierarchy improves cognitive processing in data-intensive financial visualizations
limitations: Some learners prefer distinct chromatic coding for different sectors

claim: User interface components including interactive sliders toggles and visual indicators must maintain a minimum contrast ratio of 3 to 1 against adjacent background colors
support: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast requires visual presentation of user interface components and graphical objects to have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors
limitations: Normative web standard; applies to rendered DOM elements

claim: Interactive simulation controls must be fully operable via keyboard navigation and announce dynamic value changes through ARIA live regions
support: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.1.1 Keyboard requires all functionality of the content to be operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes
limitations: Requires explicit custom keyboard bindings for slider and step controls
